content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] users. The [product_name] mobile app can be downloaded for free on iOS and Android devices through Google Play or iTunes. Key features include connection via IP address or dynamic DNS, date/time synchronization with the mobile device, reading firmware, status table display (inputs, outputs, flags, etc.), showing and editing parameters, trend visualization, and diagnostic functions. For basic connectivity, no program changes are needed. Connections can be configured via WiFi or internet, and multiple devices and user-specific labels are supported. Parameters and configuration values can be changed where permitted. Download links: Android: [url], iOS: [url].

I installed the app for iOS. I have two [product_name] units on a local network with private IPs. I set up public IPs and port forwarding on the firewall, but I can't access the devices outside the local area network. Is there something else I need to configure on the firewall?
Have you set up port forwarding for port 10001?

I have a few more questions: 1. Is it possible to create a username and password to access a [product_name] device when it has a public IP? Would it be safer to use VPN for access? 2. Has [company_name] released a web server for [product_name]? 3. Does the iPhone app allow users to control any inputs on [product_name]? Thanks for your support.
Is there a version of the app available for Windows Phone OS?

To answer your questions: Password protection isn't included in the app itself; it must be configured via the router. VPN can also be used for security. Currently, there isn't a web server available for [product_name], but [company_name] offers operator panels with built-in web servers that can integrate with [product_name]. Remote control of physical inputs isn't possible since the actual status of the controller will always override external commands, but you can control digital network inputs via the app by setting them in the program and adding their address to the monitor table. The [product_name] app for Windows smartphones is not provided by [company_name]. You may find third-party apps in the Windows Phone marketplace.

I installed the Android app on my Samsung tablet and configured the interface with IP address 192.168.1.5, assigned to [product_name]. When checking the firmware version, I get a message saying communication with the hardware is disrupted and the operation is rejected. My setup: LAN side of D-Link DIR-655 router connected via cable to [product_name] and a PC, tablet connected via WiFi. [product_name] IP: 192.168.1.5, subnet: 255.255.255.0, gateway: 192.168.1.1 (router IP). Is there something I missed? An example program would be helpful.

I use the app for multiple client projects, configuring the VM table monitor interface. Is it possible to transfer or copy the parameter list (names and addresses) from one phone to another, so I don't have to recreate VM tables each time? Or maybe save versions for adjustments? Where is the app's data stored?

On Android, look for a file named [product_name]App_date.pak. Try copying this file to another device, though I'm unsure if it works. I found the file on the memory card, but didn't see any related files in system memory. Hope this helps.

I searched for [product_name] app files on my Android but haven't found any. Which folder did you locate that file in? If the app only uses one data file, transferring all projects to another phone at once would be a problem since I'd only want to copy a single project for a client. This would be a useful feature for future releases, along with the ability to download the data log.

I've installed the [product_name] app on my SD card, and found the [product_name]App folder with three files, all named similarly. For example: App_22_Nov.apk. I assume these contain the complete configuration, including tables. However, I haven't tried copying them to another Android device.

Thanks for your response. I use a Samsung Galaxy S3 with Android 4.1.2, and couldn't install apps to the external SD card, so I can't find the files you mentioned. They seem to be stored in internal memory, which isn't accessible. Are you using an older Android version, or did you root your phone to install to SD card?
I'm using a Samsung XCover I with Android V2.3. I've attached a screenshot. Good luck.
Those are installation package files (.apk) for the [product_name] app, not data files. So transferring project data as discussed likely isn't possible at this time. Maybe in a future app version.

Great feature! How can I connect my Samsung Galaxy Note Pad to [product_name]? Do I need an Ethernet cable between [product_name] and my mobile device? I saw videos where the connection seemed wireless. Thanks!
You can connect through a standard WLAN router, that's my approach.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience issues with [product_name] app configuration, remote access setup, lack of integrated security features such as passwords, absence of web-based access, and restricted input control functions. There are also concerns about app support for various platforms (specifically Windows Phone) and challenges with transferring configuration data between devices. Connectivity problems and unclear error messages hinder troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect streamlined and secure remote connectivity to [product_name] hardware via the app, full control over inputs and outputs, web access functionality, and easy options to move or back up configuration and monitoring tables between mobile devices.
